items.q: What if I need to cancel?

items.a: I can't promise treatment will be completely pain-free. Depending on your injury and the treatment, you may feel some discomfort during or after a session. Your comfort and safety always come first: I'll explain what I'm doing as I go, keep the intensity at a level that suits your condition, and adjust straight away if anything feels too painful. Just tell me.

items.q: Do I need a GP referral?
items.a: No. You can book directly without a referral. If your assessment suggests you need input from a GP or another specialist, I'll tell you and help you understand the next step.

items.q: What happens in my first session?
items.a: We'll start by talking through your injury or goals, your activity and your history. Then I'll assess how you move: range of motion, strength and the specific area that's bothering you. You'll leave with a clear explanation of what's going on, hands-on treatment where appropriate, and a rehab plan you can start straight away.

items.q: How many sessions will I need?
items.a: It depends on the injury, how long you've had it and your goals. Some people need one or two sessions and a good home programme; others benefit from regular check-ins over a few weeks. After your assessment I'll give you an honest recommendation, never a pre-sold package.

A Sport Rehabilitator is a graduate-trained clinician who specialises in musculoskeletal injuries, rehabilitation and getting people back to sport and activity. The focus is on assessment, hands-on treatment and exercise-based rehab, from the first day of an injury right through to full performance.

items.q: I'm not an athlete. Can you still help?
items.a: Absolutely. Plenty of my clients just want to walk, garden, lift their kids or sit at a desk without pain. The same principles apply: understand the problem, treat it and build you back stronger.
You pay securely online when you book, by card, Apple Pay or Google Pay, so there's nothing to sort out on the day. Gift vouchers can be redeemed at checkout.
